held.label: Delayed
held.body: Delivery is paused for now and resumes automatically. You don't need to do anything.

list.title: Broadcasts
list.name: Name
list.emptyHint: One message to your whole audience.
list.deleteBody: "{name}" will be deleted. Drafts leave nothing behind.

composer.nameHint: Internal label. Recipients never see it.
composer.topicHint: Scopes the send and each recipient's one-click unsubscribe to this topic.
composer.switchBody: The blocks are replaced by the HTML they render, and the broadcast opens in code mode from then on. Blocks with a Show if condition are left out of that HTML. Until you save, Back to blocks undoes the switch; after that, converting back flattens the layout.
composer.segmentHint: Narrows this send to the contacts matching a saved segment.
composer.testRateLimited: Too many test emails — try again in an hour.
composer.testQueuedLimit: Test queued. {domain}'s daily limit is used up, so it goes out after 00:00 UTC.
composer.testQueued: Test queued. It goes out as soon as it can.

guard.title: Send broadcast
guard.appBaseUrl: APP_BASE_URL is not set. Unsubscribe links are built from it — set it and restart.
guard.stepStarts: starts about {time} · other sends are ahead of yours
guard.stepMoreReset: {count} more when the limit resets at {reset}
guard.stepLastReset: last {count} when the limit resets at {reset} · finishes about {time}
guard.reason: Sends above the daily sending capacity are spread over the following days. Your transactional email goes out ahead of them.
guard.limitReason: {domain} is a new domain, so it sends up to {cap} emails a day for now. A higher plan doesn't change it.
guard.planFitsOverage: {plan} with overage sends all of them by {time}
guard.tooLarge: This audience needs more than {days} days of sending capacity. Split it into smaller segments or contact support.
guard.tooLargeSelfHost: This audience needs more than {days} days of sending capacity. Split it into smaller segments or ask your instance operator for more capacity.
guard.stepFirstReset: {count} go out when the limit resets at {reset}
guard.riskNotice: {domain} has never sent more than {best, plural, one {# email} other {# emails}} in a day. Jumping to {count} is how new senders land in spam.
guard.riskNoticeNew: {domain} hasn't sent bulk email yet. Sending {count} at once is how new senders land in spam.
guard.optionWarmupSub: Most active first. {start} {when, select, today {today} other {on {day}}}, then about 1.5× a day while delivery stays healthy. Finishes about {date}.
guard.optionWarmupSubOpen: Most active first. {start} {when, select, today {today} other {on {day}}}, then about 1.5× a day while delivery stays healthy.
guard.optionNormalSub: As fast as daily capacity allows. Finishes about {date}.
guard.optionNormalSubOpen: As fast as daily capacity allows.
guard.warmingIntro: {domain} is warming up. Most active contacts go first.
guard.pausedIntro: {domain}'s warm-up is paused. This broadcast waits until it resumes.
guard.warmupReason: Mailbox providers trust a new sender a little more each day it behaves. Each day grows only while delays, bounces and complaints stay low. The warm-up never holds your transactional email.

detail.stopBody: Stop the remaining {waiting} sends? The {sent} already sent are not affected.
detail.warmupOrderSkipped: most active first · {skipped, number} inactive skipped
detail.warmupHeldBody: {reasons} Volume grows again tomorrow if it recovers.
detail.warmupPausedBody: {reasons} This broadcast waits until the domain's warm-up resumes.
detail.warmupNote: {domain} is warming up. Each day's volume grows while delivery stays healthy, most active contacts first. The warm-up never holds your transactional email.

providers.label: By inbox provider
providers.noComplaints: This provider never tells senders when someone marks mail as spam.
providers.note: Grouped by the recipient's address. Company domains hosted by Google or Microsoft count as Other.
